## The narrative

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
In this marketplace, **delivery performance drives customer satisfaction and
retention**. I *measured* it, I *predicted* it, and I *explained the voice of the
customer*.
:::

Three projects built on the same
[Olist Brazilian E-Commerce dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce)
— ~100,000 orders across nine related tables. Each project ships a report, a
one-page decision memo, and an honest statement of what the data *cannot* support.

## Projects

::: {.project-card}
### 01 · Retail Analytics <span class="status-published">· published</span>

**Question.** Which levers actually move customer satisfaction and repeat purchase?

RFM segmentation, monthly cohort retention, and a decomposition of delivery
performance — modelled with dbt on top of PostgreSQL, with data tests that fail
the build when the data stops making sense.

<p class="stack">PostgreSQL · dbt · SQL · Python · Quarto</p>

[Read the report](reports/01-retail-analytics/01-business-analytics.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-sm}
[Decision memo](reports/01-retail-analytics/00-executive-memo.qmd){.btn .btn-secondary .btn-sm}
:::

::: {.project-card}
### 02 · Late-Delivery Prediction <span class="status-wip">· in progress</span>

**Question.** At purchase time, can we tell which orders will arrive late?

A cost-sensitive classifier that is honest about leakage: only features available
*at the moment of purchase* are allowed in.

<p class="stack">Python · pandas · scikit-learn</p>
:::

::: {.project-card}
### 03 · Voice of the Customer <span class="status-wip">· planned</span>

**Question.** What do ~99,000 Portuguese-language reviews actually complain about?

Sentiment and topic modelling — with the finding that the complaints are about
*logistics*, not products, which closes the argument opened in Project 01.

<p class="stack">Python · NLP · topic modelling</p>
:::

## How this is built

Every project in this repository is reproducible from a clean clone:

```bash
uv run python tasks.py setup      # dependencies + database + dataset
uv run python tasks.py pipeline   # load -> dbt build -> tests -> render
```

The dataset is downloaded from a **revision-pinned** mirror and validated against
expected file sizes, so the numbers in these reports do not quietly change
underneath you.
